title: Grateful Dead Live at Fillmore East on 1971-04-27
lineage: SBD > MR  7 inch (7.5 ips) Revox A 77 > Alesis Masterlink 9600 > CD-R

ai_review.summary: A high‑energy April ’71 Fillmore East show highlighted by a monster Hard To Handle jam and stellar first‑set gems, captured on a solid soundboard tape despite a few missing endings.
ai_review.review: The performance is widely praised for its fire—especially the legendary Hard To Handle/The Theme sequence, tight Truckin' and Bertha, and an adventurous Beach Boys cameo.  The soundboard source is generally clear and balanced, though several reviewers note that the tape runs out during "Help Me Rhonda" and there are occasional drop‑outs, making the recording good but not flawless.

ai_rating.rationale: Average reviewer rating ≈ 4.5 (22 reviews) with consistent praise for the show; recording issues are noted but do not outweigh the musical strengths.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Generally crisp and well‑balanced soundboard mix.  Some reviewers mention tape runs out during "Help Me Rhonda" and occasional drop‑outs or missing sections from the multitrack master, but overall the audio is listenable.

standout_songs: Hard To Handle / The Theme jam
China Cat Sunflower → I Know You Rider
show_quality.setlist_flow: First set packed with pearls—Truckin', Bertha, Hard To Handle, Casey Jones—setting a high bar.  The second set adds novelty with the Beach Boys; their set slows things down briefly but the overall arc stays strong, ending abruptly on "Help Me Rhonda".

band_member_comments.Jerry: Praised for pedal‑steel work and a ripping, “eye of the tiger” guitar solo on Hard To Handle; noted chord work on Bertha.
band_member_comments.Phil: Highlighted for building tension with Lesh during The Theme jam, delivering powerful bass lines.
band_member_comments.Bob: Vocals on Casey Jones described as intense (voice cracking toward the end); solid rhythm guitar throughout.
band_member_comments.Drums: Dennis Wilson of the Beach Boys noted on "Johnny B. Goode"; overall drum foundation considered solid.
